messages:
Sam: Quick sync — RFC follow-up for migrating policy plane to a 'capability ports' model instead of the existing shared policy lib. Want alignment on rollout approach, migration safety, and metrics to watch.
Cheng: TL;DR: ports = pluggable interfaces per capability, runtime dispatch. Pros: isolation, faster per-capability iteration. Cons: more surface area, slight runtime dispatch overhead. :thinking:
Maria: Can we preserve strong compile-time checks? Runtime plugins worry me for subtle contract drift.
Maria: ```go
// idea for the port interface
type CapabilityPort interface {
  Name() string
  Evaluate(ctx context.Context, input Payload) (Result, error)
}
```
Sam: Good point. Plan is typed host interface + a lightweight shim that validates conformance at startup and via a canary harness. We avoid reflection in the hot path.
Olivia: DB migration question — existing rules live as JSON blobs. Do we need a rewrite step or adapters that map old blobs to new port payloads?
Cheng: Proposal: keep legacy runner around. Migration flow: 1) adapter shim that registers ports and delegates to legacy runner when needed; 2) dual-run mode (both old and new) for ~2 weeks with comparison metrics; 3) flip tenant-by-tenant.
Maria: Metrics to capture: eval latency p50/p95, error rate, "policy_mismatch" (old vs new), cache hit rate, and tokenized cost delta.
Sam: Also require automatic fallback to legacy runner on panic or contract error. Rollouts gated by tenant flags. Example rollout config:```json
{
  "capability_ports": {
    "enabled_for_tenants": ["tenant_a", "tenant_b"],
    "canary_percentage": 10
  }
}
```
infra-bot: deploy created: policy-ports-shim v0.1 -> staging (build 20231101)
Olivia: Running staging load test now — seeing a small perf spike (~3-5ms) under bursty evals. Need longer tail tests.
Cheng: We can optimize later: in-process registration and avoid JSON reflection on the hot path; also add a micro-batch fast-path for common trivial rules.
Maria: Request: define SLOs for the new path and add regression alarms when cost delta > 8% or p95 increases >10%.
Sam: I'll update the RFC with the canary playbook, SLOs, and the migration checklist. I'll open a follow-up PR for the shim + canary automation and assign implementation tasks to @Cheng and @Olivia.
Olivia: :thumbsup: I'll add e2e tests and a migration job to convert a small tenant's ruleset as a rehearsal.
Sam: Thanks — re-check sync on Friday to confirm cutover readiness and any blocking metrics.
